answer: Stake-weighted rate-limiting resists sybil attacks by binding each identity's message and challenge throughput to posted stake rather than to nadir count. A new address starts with near-zero quota, so flooding the network with fake identities yields almost no added bandwidth. To matter, an attacker must lock real capital behind every karst identity, and that bonded stake is slashable if the identity misbehaves.
